notes: How lab environments are built: the hypervisor, the templates, the network, and the defaults each engine is installed with.
This is the file db-ops init writes, not a sample: it is read as it stands. data/sre_config.example.json carries worked examples of the parts that ship empty.

Every key ships PRESENT and EMPTY. The shape is the product's and the answers are yours - a hypervisor path, a template name and a network are facts about your hardware, and a seed that invented them would describe a lab nobody has. Empty means the SRE app can say which field it is missing instead of failing on a path that was never real.
The password fields are refs into the encrypted secret store, never values. See data/sre_config.example.json for a worked lab.

credentials._note: Lab-only. These machines are created from a template, rehearsed on and destroyed, which is why a literal password here is defensible. Prefer the ref form anyway: write "<name>_password_ref": "SOME_STORE_KEY" and keep the value in the encrypted secret store (db-ops encrypt-secret). A literal, "<name>_password_env", and "<name>_password_ref" are all read, in that order. A lab that gets kept is how a throwaway password becomes a stored one.
